body:
_Migrated from issue #1005, filed 2026-07-19._

Found while anchoring new SPA strings for #855.

Running the documented regeneration command:

```
python scripts/extract_spa_strings.py --write
```

adds the genuinely-new msgids but also **removes about 30 anchors whose strings are still present in the frontend**. Spot-checked, all still live on `main`:

| msgid | still used in |
|---|---|
| `OAuth / OpenID Connect` | `frontend/src/pages/Admin.tsx` |
| `Clear default` | `frontend/src/pages/AdvancedSearch.tsx` |
| `begins with` | `frontend/src/components/MetadataTypeahead.tsx` |

Others dropped in the same run: `<`, `=`, `>`, `Date Added`, `LDAP`, `None`, `Publication Date`, `Dismiss help announcement`, `contains`, `is`, `is not`, `ends with`, `in the past N days`, `on or after`, `≤`, `≥`, and more — the magic-shelf rule operators among them.

## Why it matters

This is the exact failure `cps/spa_strings.py` exists to prevent. Dropping an anchor means pybabel stops seeing the msgid, `msgmerge` marks its translations obsolete, and the SPA silently falls back to English in every locale — the #577 / #719 class, which has already shipped to users twice.

It is currently latent because nobody has committed a `--write` result, but the docstring and the guard test's own failure message both tell you to run it:

```
Regenerate with: python scripts/extract_spa_strings.py --write
```

So the next person who follows the instructions regresses ~30 strings across every locale.

## Why the guard doesn't catch it

`tests/unit/test_spa_strings_anchored.py` checks `missing_anchors()` — anchors that *should* exist but don't. It has no assertion about anchors being *removed*, and the extractor can't see these strings in the first place, so they're invisible to both sides.

## Suggested fix

1. Work out why the extractor misses them (they look like data-driven / non-literal `t()` call sites, e.g. labels in option arrays and operator tables).
2. Make `--write` **additive by default** for anchors it cannot prove are dead, or require an explicit `--prune` for removals.
3. Add a guard test that fails when a regeneration would drop an existing anchor, so this can't land silently.

Workaround for now: hand-add new anchors in sorted position rather than running `--write` (what #1004 did).
title: extract_spa_strings.py --write drops ~30 msgids that are still live in .tsx
